files.preview: The deep distress our family feels because of Ney's loss in such a violent and unnecessary way is complicated by feelings of disbelief. We vote differently and we rarely completely agree on the finer details of what it means to be a citizen of this country and despite those differences we have always treated each other with love and respect. We hope that our family can be even a small example to others not to let political ideals divide us to be good like Renee. Unapologetically hopeful. That was Renee. As a mother Renee poured herself into love. The kind of love that shows up every day, that sacrifices quietly, that cheers loudly, that believes deeply. Her children were and are her heart and she made sure they felt safe, valued and endlessly loved. She believed in second chances. She believed tomorrow could be better than today. ...

files.preview: Donald Trump is just as unpopular as he was in 2018, but Democrats are still falling behind, and it's a big warning sign for the midterms. Trump's approval rating now is almost exactly what it was this time in 2018, but Democrats' lead on the generic ballot, even as it's grown from 2025, is about half what it was this time in 2018. And for some political analysts and observers, this is a really interesting dynamic. And for Republicans, it could be a real lifeline or a mirage. files.preview: I woke up one day with my name mentioned over 500 times. The government promised us over and over again that our information would be protected and properly redacted. Those promises were broken. These documents hold disturbing and yet incomplete accounts of my abuse. And they were viewable not only by the entire world, but my child, my students, my students' parents, my friends, my employers, my colleagues, my family. Husbands learned about their wives' abuse for the first time.
